proof:
Source: Step 2 ("Forms supported off L are annihilated") of the supplied proof of the selected theorem iwl_cr_ci_product_support, specialized: the slice family φ is given as data (in the selected theorem it is produced by slice_forms) and only the vanishing of ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds is proved; the product identity (Prod) is not used here.

Notation (as in the parent proof): E := ℝ^P = Eucl P and E′ := ℝ^{P+1} = Eucl (P + 1); Φ(s, x) := (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ).symm (Fin.cons s (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ x)) ∈ E′ for s ∈ ℝ, x ∈ E; e_0 := EuclideanSpace.single 0 1 ∈ E′; ι(w) := Φ(0, w) for w ∈ E; D^k(E) := TestFormOn univ k and D_k(E) := GeometricCurrentOn univ k; L := {Φ(p.1, p.2) : p ∈ [0, 1] × B̄_R(0)}, the image of Icc 0 1 ×ˢ closedBall 0 R under p ↦ Φ(p.1, p.2). Hypotheses: (H1) spt X ⊆ B̄_R(0); (H2) tsupport η and L are disjoint; (H3) φ(s)(x)(v) = η(Φ(s, x))(Fin.cons e_0 (fun i => ι(v i))) for all s ∈ [0, 1], x ∈ E and v : Fin m → E. (If R < 0 then B̄_R(0) = ∅ and L = ∅; the argument below applies verbatim.)

1. (Continuity of Φ(s, ·).) Fix s ∈ ℝ. The map x ↦ Φ(s, x) is continuous: EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin P) ℝ and (EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin (P + 1)) ℝ).symm are continuous linear equivalences, and w ↦ Fin.cons s w from Fin P → ℝ to Fin (P + 1) → ℝ is continuous (Continuous.finCons applied to the constant map s and the identity: coordinate 0 is the constant s and coordinate j + 1 is w_j).
2. (The sets C_s and N_s.) Fix s ∈ [0, 1] and put C_s := {x ∈ E : Φ(s, x) ∈ tsupport η} and N_s := E ∖ C_s = {x ∈ E : Φ(s, x) ∉ tsupport η}. Since tsupport η is closed (isClosed_tsupport), C_s is closed as the preimage of a closed set under the continuous map of step 1; hence N_s is open.
3. (B̄_R(0) ⊆ N_s.) Let x ∈ E with ‖x‖ ≤ R, i.e. x ∈ closedBall 0 R. Then (s, x) ∈ [0, 1] × B̄_R(0), so Φ(s, x) ∈ L. By (H2), Φ(s, x) ∉ tsupport η, i.e. x ∈ N_s.
4. (φ(s) vanishes on N_s, hence tsupport φ(s) ⊆ C_s.) Let x ∈ N_s. Then Φ(s, x) ∉ tsupport η, so η(Φ(s, x)) = 0 as a covector (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). By (H3), which applies because s ∈ [0, 1], for every v : Fin m → E we get φ(s)(x)(v) = η(Φ(s, x))(Fin.cons e_0 (fun i => ι(v i))) = 0, so φ(s)(x) = 0 as a continuous alternating map (extensionality). Thus support φ(s) ⊆ C_s, and since C_s is closed (step 2), tsupport φ(s) = closure (support φ(s)) ⊆ C_s (closure_minimal).
5. (X(φ(s)) = 0.) Suppose x ∈ tsupport φ(s) and x ∈ spt X. By (H1), x ∈ B̄_R(0), so x ∈ N_s by step 3; but x ∈ C_s by step 4, contradicting N_s = E ∖ C_s. Hence tsupport φ(s) and spt X are disjoint, and vanish_off_support (applied with P, n := m, U := univ, T := X, ω := φ(s)) gives X(φ(s)) = 0.
6. (The integral vanishes.) By step 5, X(φ(s)) = 0 for every s ∈ [0, 1], and uIcc 0 1 = [0, 1] because 0 ≤ 1 (uIcc_of_le). So the integrands s ↦ X(φ(s)) and s ↦ 0 agree on uIcc 0 1, and intervalIntegral.integral_congr gives ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds = ∫_0^1 0 ds = 0 (intervalIntegral.integral_zero). ∎
key_steps: For fixed s, x ↦ Φ(s, x) is continuous, so C_s = {x : Φ(s, x) ∈ tsupport η} is closed and N_s = E ∖ C_s is open.
For s ∈ [0, 1], B̄_R(0) ⊆ N_s, because Φ(s, x) ∈ L whenever ‖x‖ ≤ R and tsupport η misses L.
By the slice identity and η = 0 off tsupport η, φ(s) vanishes on N_s, so tsupport φ(s) ⊆ C_s (closure_minimal).
spt X ⊆ B̄_R(0) ⊆ N_s, so tsupport φ(s) is disjoint from spt X and X(φ(s)) = 0 by vanish_off_support.
The integrand vanishes on uIcc 0 1 = [0, 1], so ∫_0^1 X(φ(s)) ds = 0 by intervalIntegral.integral_congr.
